stem: A child has a smooth plastic bead in the ear canal and office irrigation is being considered; what must be checked before irrigating?

options.text: That the tympanic membrane is intact
That the child already has decreased hearing
That there is a draining node on the mastoid tip
That soothing dressings have been tried

explanation: Tympanic membrane integrity must be confirmed before ear canal irrigation. Irrigation may be used for some ear foreign bodies, but only if the tympanic membrane is intact.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Correct because the tympanic membrane must be intact before irrigation to reduce the risk of middle ear injury or complications.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because decreased hearing is not the safety check required before irrigating an ear foreign body.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because a draining node on the mastoid tip is not the relevant pre-irrigation assessment.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because canal itch is not the prerequisite that must be checked before irrigation.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because soothing dressings are not required before irrigating an ear canal foreign body.
